title: Cellular Biology Practice Exam
description: 15-question practice exam covering cell structure, organelles, membrane transport, and mitosis

questions.question: Which of the following structures is found in prokaryotic cells but NOT in eukaryotic cells?
questions.explanation: The nucleoid is a DNA-containing region in prokaryotic cells that is NOT enclosed by a membrane. Eukaryotic cells have a true membrane-bound nucleus instead. All cells have cell membranes, and mitochondria are found only in eukaryotic cells.

questions.question: Which organelle is responsible for packaging and shipping proteins and lipids to their final destinations?
questions.explanation: The Golgi apparatus functions as the 'post office' of the cell, receiving products from the rough ER, modifying them, and packaging them into vesicles for transport to their final destinations. The rough ER synthesizes proteins; lysosomes digest waste; the nucleolus makes ribosomes.

questions.question: A red blood cell is placed in a hypertonic saline solution. What will happen to the cell?
options: The cell will swell due to water influx (lysis)
The cell will shrivel due to water efflux (crenation)
No change will occur; the solution is isotonic
questions.explanation: In a hypertonic solution, water concentration is lower outside the cell than inside, so water moves out by osmosis. This causes the cell to lose volume and shrivel, developing a spiky appearance called crenation. The cell will not burst because it's losing water, not gaining it.

questions.question: True or False: Mitochondria contain their own DNA and are thought to have originated from free-living prokaryotes.
questions.explanation: This is true. Mitochondria have their own circular DNA (mtDNA) and are believed to have originated through endosymbiosis—a prokaryotic cell was engulfed by an early eukaryotic cell and became an organelle. This is strong evidence for the endosymbiotic theory.

questions.question: True or False: During metaphase, chromosomes are located at the cell poles, ready to be pulled toward the equator.
questions.explanation: False. During metaphase, chromosomes are aligned AT the equator (the metaphase plate), not at the poles. This alignment is the defining characteristic of metaphase. The spindle poles are where the centrioles/centrosomes are located.

questions.question: Which phase of mitosis is characterized by the breakdown of the nuclear envelope and condensation of chromatin into visible chromosomes?
questions.explanation: Prophase is the first phase of mitosis during which chromatin condenses into visible chromosomes and the nuclear envelope breaks down. The spindle apparatus also begins to form during prophase. Metaphase follows, during which chromosomes align at the equator.

questions.question: Active transport differs from facilitated diffusion in that active transport:
options: Moves substances against their concentration gradient using ATP energy
Is found only in prokaryotic cells
Can move substances through the cell wall
questions.explanation: Active transport moves substances against their concentration gradient (from low to high concentration) and requires ATP energy. Facilitated diffusion also uses transport proteins but moves substances DOWN the concentration gradient without requiring ATP. Both are found in both cell types.

questions.question: True or False: Plant cells contain lysosomes for digesting cellular waste, just like animal cells do.
questions.explanation: False. Plant cells typically lack lysosomes. Instead, they have a large central vacuole that stores digestive enzymes and performs similar digestive functions. Animal cells have numerous lysosomes throughout the cytoplasm.

questions.question: The process by which water moves across a semipermeable membrane from an area of low solute concentration to an area of high solute concentration is called ___________.
questions.explanation: Osmosis is the specific term for the diffusion of water molecules across a semipermeable membrane. It is driven by differences in solute concentration, with water moving toward the region of higher solute concentration (hypertonic solution).

questions.question: The _____________ apparatus is the site where ribosomal RNA is synthesized and ribosomal subunits are assembled within the nucleus.
questions.explanation: The nucleolus is a dense region within the nucleus where ribosomal RNA (rRNA) is synthesized and ribosomal subunits (40S and 60S) are assembled. The nucleolus is not membrane-bound and is most active in cells with high protein synthesis rates.

questions.question: A muscle cell contains significantly more mitochondria than a skin cell. This is because:
options: Muscle cells require more energy to perform contraction
Skin cells have more lysosomes instead
Mitochondria are toxic in skin cells
questions.explanation: Mitochondria produce ATP through cellular respiration. Muscle cells require large amounts of ATP for muscle contraction, so they contain many more mitochondria than low-energy cells like skin fibroblasts. The number of mitochondria reflects a cell's energy demands.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the cell membrane is CORRECT?
options: It is composed primarily of a triglyceride monolayer
It is selectively permeable, controlling what enters and exits the cell
It is found only in eukaryotic cells
It allows all molecules to pass through equally
questions.explanation: The cell membrane is a phospholipid bilayer that is selectively permeable—small nonpolar molecules pass easily, while large polar molecules require transport proteins or energy. It is found in ALL cells (both prokaryotic and eukaryotic), not just eukaryotes. It does not allow all molecules to pass equally.

questions.question: Explain why a plant cell placed in a hypotonic solution becomes turgid rather than bursting, while an animal cell placed in the same solution would likely burst (lyse).
questions.model_answer: Plant cells have a rigid cell wall that provides structural support and prevents the cell from expanding indefinitely. When water enters the cell by osmosis in a hypotonic solution, the cell membrane pushes against the cell wall, creating turgor pressure that keeps the plant firm without rupturing. Animal cells lack a cell wall, so when water enters, the cell swells until the cell membrane ruptures (lysis).
questions.explanation: This question tests understanding of osmosis, turgor pressure, and the structural differences between plant and animal cells. Key concepts: plant cell wall limits expansion, turgor pressure, and the consequence of osmotic imbalance in cells lacking a cell wall.

questions.question: Describe what happens during anaphase of mitosis and explain why this phase is critical for accurate cell division.
questions.model_answer: During anaphase, sister chromatids separate at the centromere and are pulled toward opposite poles of the cell by shortening spindle fibers. This phase is critical because it ensures that each daughter cell receives an identical, complete set of chromosomes. If sister chromatids fail to separate properly (nondisjunction), one daughter cell will have extra chromosomes and the other will have missing chromosomes, leading to genetic abnormalities.
questions.explanation: This question assesses understanding of chromosome movement during mitosis and the importance of accurate chromosome segregation. Key concepts: sister chromatid separation, spindle fiber function, and the consequence of errors (nondisjunction).

questions.question: True or False: DNA replication occurs during mitosis (M phase), ensuring that each daughter cell receives a full copy of the genetic material.
questions.explanation: False. DNA replication occurs during the S (synthesis) phase of interphase, which occurs BEFORE mitosis. By the time mitosis begins, DNA has already been replicated. Mitosis simply distributes the already-replicated chromosomes to daughter cells. This is a common misconception on exams.
